turns.t: Hello, I'm Tia, I'll weigh and measure Evie later if the doctor wants. Take a seat, they won't be long. ~
Thanks, love. We've been waiting ages. Evie, don't scratch. ~
Hello, I'm Dr Pearson. Evie, how old are you? ~
Nine. ~
Nine, lovely. Evie, what's wrong with your head?
It's itchy. And there's white stuff.
Flaky white bits in her hair, doctor, on her shoulders, her school jumper. And she scratches at night.
When did it start, Evie?
Two weeks.
It's longer than that, love, it's two months at least. I remember because of the half-term.
So two weeks from Evie and two months from Mum. I'll write that down. Does anyone else at home have itchy heads?
Her little brother scratches. I've not looked properly. ~
Has she had any hair loss, patches where hair's gone?
No, no bald patches. Her hair's thick, thankfully.
Any sore, weepy or crusty bits on the scalp?
No, nothing weepy. Just flaky and red in places.
Evie, can I look at your scalp? Bend your head forward. ~
Okay.
There are fine white flakes and some redness around the hair roots, mostly at the back and behind the ears. No broken hairs, and no bald spots.
Is it nits? ~
I can't see lice or eggs. I'd say this looks like a dry, flaky scalp, but I can't rule out a fungal infection, which is more likely to spread between children.
Ringworm? ~
It's possible, so I'd like to take a few flakes and a couple of hairs for testing. It doesn't hurt.
Will it hurt? ~
No, Evie, it's like a gentle brush.
Doctor, shall I label the sample? ~
Please, Tia. Mum, I'll also look at her brother's head when you next come. ~
Okay. ~
Meanwhile, use a gentle shampoo, don't scratch, and don't share hats or combs.
Right. ~
If bald patches appear, the scalp gets crusty or sore, or the neck glands swell, come back and see me.
We will. Thank you. ~
Bye. ~
